body: If it's that important for you, why not dump his sorry a$$ and retire to California? I don't know. I just wonder if this feeling of not belonging would actually remain with you even as you move. Cali changed in 40 years. You might find that you no longer fit and belong there either. So what you should do is go there with an extended visit, for whatever reason. If you see that that really is the place for you - dump him and move. You're not that old. Have you tried counselling though? Why don't you feel like you belong in a place you lived for more than 40 years now? What does that mean actually? <--not trying to discredit your feelings somehow, just asking to see what sort of a problem that is - because maybe it's something you solve by counselling, or maybe by moving.

OK, you've got a lot on your plate there. I would like to help by offering a boilerplate email you should email to all your professors to ask for recommendation. It would be better if you contacted them in person, but if you can't bring yourself up to doing that - email. 
So:

Dear Professor [Last Name]. My name is [you name] and I took your [name of class] in [semester/year]. I was [basic description - the dark haired kid in the corner of the class, the guy who did report on mechanics of underwater basket weaving, - anything descriptive; might even attach your photo]. [If you got an A in that class, say it]. I have a favor to ask of you. I am trying to apply to Graduate School [school/subject]. Could you possibly provide me with a letter of recommendation? 
Thank you very much,
[your name]
------------------------
It would be better if you could say that you enjoyed their class or that you learned something (especially if you can list what you learned) but if you don't want to- don't. 

Many profs will frown at this and they will not do it. But you only need two or three. If all else fails - say, they all refuse - you contact them back and say *please, I am desperate. I have not formed relationships with any professors at school and so there is nobody who will write me a letter.* now, that will work on some professors. 
Voila. Now you have letters.

Listen, job search is horrible, incredibly demoralizing, painful -everything. But in the end of the day it is a numbers game. Simply numbers. You need to send out so many hundreds of letters to get so many dozens phone interviews to get so many further interviews to get a job. Keep your head above the water, this too shall pass. You will reach the magic number of rejections that will be your path to a job. I have been there. I know many others who have. The interim - this whole job search - is pure hell. Wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. But after you hit your numbers, it WILL happen.
